name: NTUSER.DAT (User Registry Hive)
os_min: Windows 2000 (present in all NT-based Windows versions)
location: Mounted as HKEY_CURRENT_USER while the user is logged on; also reachable as HKEY_USERS\<SID> for a non-interactive profile. File: %UserProfile%\NTUSER.DAT (e.g. C:\Users\<username>\NTUSER.DAT)
purpose: Root of a single user's registry — mounted as HKEY_CURRENT_USER for the duration of that user's session. Holds per-user application settings and UI preferences and, forensically, a per-user Run/RunOnce autostart location. User-activity artifacts that also live in this hive — UserAssist, RunMRU, TypedPaths, RecentDocs — are documented as separate artifacts; this entry covers the hive's general role and its own persistence keys.
key_fields: Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and \RunOnce — per-user autostart entries, executed only when that specific user logs on
Software\Classes — per-user COM/file-association overrides layered on top of HKLM\SOFTWARE\Classes (the underlying per-user Classes data itself is stored in the separate UsrClass.dat hive)
Volatile Environment — session-specific environment variables (e.g. USERNAME, USERDOMAIN, logon server) recreated at each logon
Hive last-write time and the paired NTUSER.DAT.LOG1/.LOG2 transaction logs
normal_baseline: Per-user Run entries correspond to user-installed, signed applications (chat clients, cloud-sync apps); the hive's last-write time tracks with the account's actual last logoff or sync cycle.
anomalies: A per-user Run/RunOnce entry pointing to a script or binary the profile owner denies installing, especially one staged in %AppData%\Roaming or %AppData%\Local.

NTUSER.DAT's last-write time falling outside any interactive logon recorded for that account in the Security event log, suggesting the hive was modified offline or via a remote/administrative technique rather than by the user themselves.

An NTUSER.DAT file present under a user-profile folder with no corresponding account in the SAM (or SECURITY domain-cache) — an orphaned profile from a deleted account, or vice versa, a profile folder with no NTUSER.DAT.
anti_forensic_notes: NTUSER.DAT is fully flushed to disk at logoff or periodic sync; a copy acquired live from a still-logged-on session can miss the most recent writes still held in the in-memory hive unless the .LOG1/.LOG2 transaction logs are also collected and replayed. Deleting a user profile removes NTUSER.DAT from its normal location, but Windows.old, Volume Shadow Copies, or backup/roaming-profile stores can retain earlier copies.
